title: Research Dataset for Immune-Related Adverse Events Affecting the Central Nervous System
projectDescription: This dataset contains all research data collected for irAE-CNS conducted between 2019.1 and 2024.9. The collection includes files comprising experimental measurements, survey responses, processed analyses. Data formats include CSV, RDATA, and Excel. The complete dataset is organized into categories. All files follow consistent naming conventions and include detailed metadata describing collection methods, instruments/settings used, and processing steps.
sampleProcessingProtocol: The core challenge in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) sample processing lies in its extremely low protein content and significant interference from a small number of highly abundant proteins. The procedure begins immediately after clinical collection, requiring prompt centrifugation, aliquoting, and storage at -80°C to prevent degradation. Prior to analysis, samples must undergo concentration (e.g., via ultrafiltration) and are typically subjected to affinity depletion to remove high-abundance proteins like albumin and immunoglobulins, thereby unveiling more low-abundance proteins of potential interest. Subsequently, the samples are processed through reduction, alkylation, and enzymatic digestion to generate peptide mixtures, followed by desalting and purification, ultimately preparing them for mass spectrometry analysis.
dataProcessingProtocol: Data analysis commences with searching the raw mass spectrometry data against protein databases to identify proteins and perform quantification. This is followed by rigorous statistical analysis and quality control, which involves handling missing values, correcting for batch effects, identifying outlier samples, and applying statistical tests to pinpoint differentially expressed proteins across sample groups. Finally, functional enrichment analysis and interrogation of brain tissue-specific expression databases are employed to interpret the biological significance, associated pathways, and relevance to the central nervous system of these differential proteins, thereby transforming data into actionable biological insights.
